chunks.title: Supplier Payment Run Procedure.docx
chunks.text:
## 5. Steps for each run

- Match. By the cut-off, each invoice is matched in NetSuite to its purchase order and goods receipt. If the invoice differs from the PO by more than 2% or £50, whichever is lower, put it on hold and query it with the supplier.

- Build the proposal. At 09:00 on the run day, Luis Ortega runs the AP-Proposal saved search, removes held invoices and checks due dates.

- Check for duplicates. Look for the same invoice number from the same supplier, and for the same supplier and amount within 60 days. Remove anything doubtful.

- Review and input. Grace Adeyemi reviews the proposal, saves it as a PDF in /Finance/AP/Payment runs, and inputs the payment file: Faster Payments for GBP, SEPA credit transfer for EUR. Use CHAPS only for a GBP payment over £1,000,000 or an urgent same-day payment approved by the Financial Controller.

- Release. The releaser checks the bank file total against the proposal and releases it by 14:00. The bank portal enforces dual control: the inputter cannot release.

- Remittance. NetSuite emails remittance advice to suppliers automatically.

- Post and reconcile. Record the bank file reference in NetSuite on the same day. The payments are matched in the next morning's bank reconciliation.

chunks.text:
## 4. Approval limits

Each invoice needs approval to pay at the level below, based on its gross amount. Non-GBP amounts are converted at the finance system's daily rate on the run date. These limits come from the delegated authority matrix (version 4, effective 1 January 2026).

| Gross amount of a single invoice or payment | Approver |
| --- | --- |
| Up to £10,000 | AP Specialist (Grace Adeyemi) |
| £10,000.01 to £50,000 | Financial Controller (Tom Whitfield) |
| £50,000.01 to £250,000 | CFO (Daniel Reyes) |
| Over £250,000 | CFO and CEO (Daniel Reyes and Amara Okafor) |

Approval to pay is separate from approval to spend. The budget holder must already have approved the spend on the purchase order or the invoice.

A run whose total is over £500,000 must be released by the CFO, whatever the size of the individual payments.

chunks.text:
## 6. New suppliers and changes to bank details

Changes to bank details are the most common way fraudsters steal from finance teams. Treat every request as suspicious until it is verified.

- New suppliers are set up on form AP-03 with the company number, VAT number and bank details on the supplier's letterhead. AP checks the company at Companies House (or the national register) and screens it against the sanctions lists.

- Any change to bank details must be verified by phone. Call the supplier on a number we already hold, never on a number given in the request, and the call must be made by someone other than the person who received the request. Record who you spoke to, when, and on which number.

- Cooling-off: new details take effect two working days after verification.

- Confirmation of Payee: run it for every new or changed GBP account. If the name does not match, stop and escalate to Tom Whitfield.

- First payment to new details: if it is over £10,000, it needs Financial Controller approval even if the amount would otherwise fall in the AP Specialist's band.

- Email-only requests to change bank details are reported the same day to Tom Whitfield and to Lena Fischer (Security Engineer), with the original email attached.

chunks.text:
## 6. Technical integration

- Authentication. Each Brightwell customer connects their Kestrel account through OAuth 2.0. Brightwell requests the scopes payouts:write and accounts:read only.

- Pay runs. Brightwell submits one Kestrel payout batch per pay run. The batch reference is the Brightwell pay run ID, so a pay run can never be submitted twice (Kestrel returns KP-5017 for a duplicate).

- Idempotency. Each payout uses the pay run ID plus the employee ID as its idempotency key.

- Cut-off. Pay runs must reach Kestrel by 15:00 UK time on the business day before pay day.

- Confirmation of Payee. Brightwell shows KP-5003 (no match) and KP-5004 (close match) to the payroll admin before pay day, so they can correct the employee's details.

- Webhooks. Brightwell listens for payout.paid, payout.failed and payout.held, and shows the status against each employee.

- Rate limits. Brightwell keeps below 25 requests a second per customer on Payouts endpoints.
